title: Al-A'la: the one who purifies
hookLine: successful is the one who purifies, remembers and prays, though you prefer this life (87:14–17)
last: AL-A'LA — GLORY TO THE MOST HIGH.

lines: ONE COOKIE NOW, OR TWO LATER?
NOW IS LOUD. LATER IS QUIET.
cards: A child at a kitchen table, one cookie on a plate. The deal: eat it now, or wait a little while and get two. Then the squirming starts.
Eyes covered. Humming. A finger edging toward the plate.
Grown-ups play the same game with money, sleep and phones, just less visibly. Now is loud. Later is quiet.
Al-A'la names that pull. First it says who succeeds, and then, with an honesty that's almost tender, it admits what people actually prefer. Today: the one who purifies.

teach.b: Verse fourteen: successful is the one who purifies himself. The verb is tazakka, from z-k-y, the root met ten days ago in Ash-Shams: successful is the one who purifies the soul.
The same root as zakat: to cleanse, and to grow. Verse fifteen adds two more: he remembers the name of his Lord, and he prays. Purify, remember, pray.
That's the whole description of success. Then verse sixteen turns to the listener, and doesn't scold.
It just says: but you prefer the life of this world. It's true, and the surah knows it. Then verse seventeen, in Pickthall's words: "Although the Hereafter is better and more lasting."
The key word is abqa, more lasting, from a root meaning to remain. It doesn't say this world is worthless. It says the later lasts longer.

teach.h: IN THE SCROLLS OF IBRAHIM AND MUSA.
teach.b: Verses eighteen and nineteen add a surprise: this is in the earlier scrolls, the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa. Nothing new; Ibrahim and Musa were told the same.
That closes a long stretch of the path.
Since day one hundred seventy-seven, it has walked backward through the middle of the thirtieth part: the earthquake that reports, the clear proof, the Night of Power, the first word, read.
The fig and the olive, the opened chest, the morning, the night, the sun and the soul, the steep path, the dawn, the overwhelming, and the Most High.
Tomorrow come the opening surahs of the juz', still walking backward toward its first page.

how: Muslims often recite Al-A'la in the Friday, Eid and witr prayers; its verses on the one who purifies himself and on the Hereafter being more lasting are often quoted in sermons and reminders.

o: the earlier scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa
the Most High, a name of God in Surah 87
the one who purifies and gives zakat

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
p: purified himself, same root as zakat

s: Al-A'la says this world is worthless
it says the Hereafter is better and more lasting, not that this world counts for nothing.
the surah says its message was already in the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa
87:18–19: this is in the earlier scrolls.
tazakka shares a root with zakat
z-k-y: to purify and to grow, as in Ash-Shams.

games.q: Al-A'la describes the successful person, then turns to the listener. what does it say the listener prefers?
games.why: but you prefer the life of the world, although the Hereafter is better and more lasting (87:16–17). honest, not scolding.

practice: Look at the choices ahead of you today: what you'll eat, what you'll watch, how you'll spend the evening, what you'll say to someone. Find one place where now and later pull in different directions.
Don't solve them all; pick that one, and decide now which way it goes.

wordCard.voice: Al-A'la. The Most High, Surah eighty-seven: success is purifying, remembering, praying, and what comes later is more lasting. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "more lasting," from b-q-y, to remain; the Hereafter is khayrun wa abqa, better and more lasting (87:17).

carryVoice: Your line: the later lasts. Purify, remember, pray. A whole stretch of the path, walked.

sources.q: Although the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
